report.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression

deepseek_report_section_5_1_2.title: RL in Synthesized Tasks
factual_findings: Rollout execution decoupled into an agent sandbox (scaffold + tools) and worker container (scaffold-agnostic control layer, normalizes interactions into common trajectory schema, communicates with trainer on DSec).
Long-lived rollouts and fine-grained GPU training scheduling are separated; during trainer preemption, rollout execution is suspended and offloaded with full state preserved for resumption.
Model merging across runs and configurations aggregates parallel RL compute across heterogeneous scaffolds.
Scales along two dimensions: training compute (cumulative RL steps) and number of scaffolds.
deepseek_report_section_5_1_2.harness_relevance: Decoupled rollout/control architecture isolates harness execution state from inference scheduling; resumption depends on complete state capture.

deepseek_report_section_5_3_4.title: Performance across agent scaffolds
factual_findings: Evaluated 8 configurations across 6 scaffold families: Claude Code (v2.1.251), Codex (v0.147.0), OpenCode (v1.18.15), Pi (v0.84.2), mini-SWE (commit 04d809ceab9d), and DeepSeek Harness (Minimal, Standard, PTC modes).
Shared evaluation settings: Linux task containers, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, 1M-token context window, max_steps=500 model-generation rounds per agent.
DeepSWE v1.1 evaluated at N=8 samples per task; Terminal-Bench v2.1 evaluated at N=3 samples per task without network access.

Reported Pass@1 / Resolved at Max reasoning effort (100): DeepSWE v1.1 resolved mini-SWE 74.2%, DSH Minimal 72.6%, DSH Standard 70.5%, Claude Code 69.8%, DSH PTC 67.6%, Pi 66.2%, Codex 65.6%, OpenCode 65.5%; Terminal-Bench v2.1 Pass@1 DSH Minimal 90.6%, mini-SWE 90.3%, Claude Code 88.0%, Pi 86.1%, DSH Standard 85.8%, DSH PTC 85.8%, OpenCode 85.0%, Codex 84.1%.
deepseek_report_section_5_3_4.harness_relevance: Demonstrates that scaffold choice introduces substantial variance under identical model weights, context window, and sampling hyperparameters.

deepseek_report_appendix_b.title: Evaluation Details

B.1.title: Scaffold Configurations
details: All scaffolds run in Linux task containers using shared settings without experimental system prompt additions.
Claude Code (v2.1.105, v2.1.238, v2.1.251, v2.1.259): uses Claude Agent SDK with native tool interface.
Codex (v0.147.0): standard app-server mode with adapted tool schemas.
OpenCode (v1.18.15): build agent with shell and file tools, and native task delegation.
Pi (v0.84.2): RPC mode with file and shell tools plus search extension (search, open_page, find_in_page).
mini-SWE: mini_swe_v2 port (commit 04d809ceab9df28f9adaed044884180159172930) with single bash tool, requiring tool call each turn and submission marker to finish.

DeepSeek Harness (DSH): Minimal mode has single persistent bash tool; Standard mode has full SDK profile with 26 initial function tools; PTC mode uses run_code for TypeScript with 24 underlying tools. Standard and PTC require custom build v0.1.1+custom.202609011522.

B.2.title: Reasoning Efforts across Scaffolds
details: Output tokens scale monotonically with reasoning effort (b=25..100) across all scaffolds and benchmarks.
Accuracy (Pass@1) does not scale monotonically; exhibits plateaus and non-monotonic dips at intermediate settings.
Scaffolds calibrate differently: Claude Code has flattest token curve; DSH Minimal gains most at highest token cost; mini-SWE is intermediate.

B.3.title: Detailed Results of Reasoning Benchmarks
details: Smooth continuous control of response length (2.0-3.1x scaling from effort 25 to 100) on single-response reasoning.
Transfer of effort knob to long-horizon agentic rollouts governs total exploration/verification turns.

deepseek_report_appendix_b.harness_relevance: Pins the exact tool surface, turn-taking rules, and effort scaling behavior for each scaffold.

deepseek_report_section_5_3_1_mitigation.title: Evaluation Setup & Anti-Gaming Mitigations
factual_findings: Automated purging of transient build/package caches: Go module caches (go/mod), node_modules dependency artifacts, compiled .jar files, and Python __pycache__ directories.
Git histories stripped from environment and internet access disabled for coding benchmarks.

Official benchmark harness coupling: DeepSWE v1.1 evaluated with mini-SWE harness to match official setup; SEC-Bench Pro uses Claude Code specifically for session compaction design; Visual agent uses Claude Code with 512k context.
deepseek_report_section_5_3_1_mitigation.harness_relevance: Environment sanitization alters filesystem discovery and build artifacts, introducing silent reproduction gaps if omitted.

pinned_mechanisms.shell_persistence: Persistent bash tool (@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash-persistent) retains state and working directory across command calls and user turns.
pinned_mechanisms.shell_timeout: Command execution timeout set to 300,000 ms (5 minutes).
pinned_mechanisms.shell_prompt_instruction: Explicitly instructs agent: 'State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user... Please avoid commands that may produce a very large amount of output... Please run long lived commands in the background, e.g. sleep 10 &'.
pinned_mechanisms.observation_clipping: Current Minimal implementation clips command output at 16,000 characters; output is not unbounded.
pinned_mechanisms.permissions_policy: danger-full-access with workspaceRoot set to process.cwd().
pinned_mechanisms.token_limit_policy: maxTokensAsSuccess: false configured on sdk-jsonrpc-server; hitting token limits does not record success.
pinned_mechanisms.session_persistence: @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl persists session event stream to JSONL files.

pinned_mechanisms.shell_persistence: Stateless subshell per action; directory (cd) and environment variable changes are NOT persistent across turns. Requires inline compounding: MY_ENV=val cd ... && ...
pinned_mechanisms.stopping_mechanism: Explicit submission marker required: 'echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT'. No further commands accepted once issued.
pinned_mechanisms.length_cutoff_handling: Detects finish_reason == 'length' and warns agent: 'Your previous response reached the output token limit... Respond more concisely and finish with exactly one bash tool call.'

reproduction_gaps.description: DeepSeek Harness Standard and PTC modes require custom proprietary build v0.1.1+custom.202609011522 not published in public releases or npm.
reproduction_gaps.impact: Standard and PTC configurations cannot be directly executed in standard open-source environments without vendor-provided binary assets. However, unverified historical custom builds do not make all future counterfactual ablations impossible, as open Minimal configurations or clean-room mechanism implementations remain testable.

reproduction_gaps.description: DeepSeek runs rollouts on DSec with custom non-Kubernetes placement engines, Sub-NUMA VM resource partitioning, and latency-sensitive SCHED_IDLE scheduling at 2,500 containers/node.
reproduction_gaps.impact: Standard Harbor or local Docker runners operate without NUMA confinement or core scheduling, causing different latency and I/O noise characteristics.

reproduction_gaps.description: Neither DeepSeek Harness nor mini-SWE ships a native Harbor adapter; historical runs rely on retrospective JSONL-to-ATIF or stdout conversion.
reproduction_gaps.impact: Converting session logs after execution can lose intermediate unbuffered terminal events or conflate harness wrappers with agent decisions.

reproduction_gaps.description: DeepSeek evaluation automatically purges Go module caches, node_modules, compiled .jar files, and __pycache__ while stripping git histories.
reproduction_gaps.impact: Benchmark tasks evaluated in standard environments without automated cache purging may leak pre-cached dependencies or git commit messages.

reproduction_gaps.description: DeepSWE v1.1 is coupled to mini-SWE (74.2%) while SEC-Bench Pro is coupled to Claude Code for session compaction (62.8%).
reproduction_gaps.impact: Direct cross-harness ranking on historical trajectories confounds scaffold-specific prompt engineering and tool interfaces with underlying agent reasoning capability.

limitations: Pinned configuration values represent specific committed snapshots and published report sections, not permanent truths about current or future harness releases.
Observational markers from historical trajectories provide correlational evidence only; causal claims require controlled counterfactual ablation.

Reproduction gaps document structural differences between published evaluation platforms and local lab capabilities; unverified custom historical builds do not make future counterfactual ablations impossible.
Proposals must not fabricate synthetic benchmark task IDs or profile IDs, and observational diagnostics do not constitute evidence of causality.
